note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits.

problems.original_statement: Specifying a target trial prevents the temporal biases an analyst inflicts on themselves; it does not create randomization. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurements all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing exchangeability. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, exist separately and are not part of any standard emulation workflow: there is no agreed order in which to apply them, no convention for reporting what each one bought, and no accepted way to combine their answers when they disagree. Covariate balance continues to be reported as though it bore on unmeasured confounding, which it does not.
problems.correction_note: The entry asked for an agreed order in which to apply these tools. There cannot be one: they identify under distinct, partly untestable assumptions and sometimes target different estimands, so they cannot be mechanically ordered or combined without an explicit estimand-aligned joint model. The missing thing is that joint model, not a sequence.
problems.statement: A correctly implemented emulation prevents specific design-induced temporal biases and does not create exchangeability. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurement all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing it. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, identify under distinct and partly untestable assumptions and sometimes target different estimands. They therefore cannot be mechanically ordered or combined: doing so requires an explicit joint model aligned to one estimand, and no such model is in use, so there is no convention for reporting what each tool contributed or for reconciling them when they disagree. Balance on measured covariates continues to be reported as though it bore on unmeasured confounding, and it does not.
problems.why_open: Combining these tools is not a matter of adding evidence but of reconciling incompatible identification stories, and the joint model that would do it has to commit to one estimand, which discards the reason several tools were used. A negative control shares only some of the confounding mechanisms of the primary outcome, and how much is not knowable from the data. Proximal methods need proxies satisfying completeness-type conditions that cannot be checked, and weak proxies produce instability that reads as precision loss rather than assumption failure. Validation subsamples are rarely random, which imports a second selection problem into the correction for the first.
problems.proposed_direction: Build an estimand-aligned joint model in which the proxies, negative controls and validation data enter as components of one identification argument, rather than seeking an order in which to apply them separately. Declare the treatment-inducing and outcome-inducing proxies and the negative controls in the protocol, and report the conventional estimate alongside E-values, bias functions, Rosenbaum-style sensitivity models, tipping-point analyses and priors on unmeasured confounding, all keyed to the same estimand so a reader sees one quantity under several assumption sets. Establish by simulation how far negative-control calibration transfers when the control shares only part of the confounding structure, which is the assumption the method makes and never states.

problems.original_statement: A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, and then a sensitivity analysis that relaxes one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data all of them are doubtful simultaneously: unmeasured confounding, selection into the cohort, misclassification of exposure and outcome, and practical positivity failure all operate at once and interact. There is little theory for the joint case, so the reported uncertainty is a sampling interval around a point that is identified only under a conjunction the analysis has already conceded is false. What is missing is a way to report an identification region reflecting all the violations together, separately from the sampling interval.
problems.correction_note: Theory and software for joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection and misclassification do exist, and some longitudinal sequential-confounding sensitivity models with them, so the claim that there is little theory for the joint case was too broad. Two things also have to be said about the joint region: it needs compatible bias parameters, dependence restrictions, a stated target population and estimand, and without those restrictions the resulting bounds can be vacuous.
problems.statement: A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, then a sensitivity analysis relaxing one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data several are doubtful at once, and one-at-a-time analyses need not characterize their joint effect. Joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection and misclassification exists, with software, and so do longitudinal sensitivity models for sequential confounding. What is not standard, and not required by any reporting practice, is a joint region that also includes practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods, with the product of marginal analyses remaining the default in practice. Constructing one requires compatible bias parameters, restrictions on how the biases depend on each other, and a stated target population and estimand; without those restrictions the resulting bounds can be vacuous, and the partial-identification set has to be reported as distinct from finite-sample uncertainty.
problems.why_open: Bias parameters for different violations live on different scales and enter the estimating equations at different points, so there is no natural single-parameter family to sweep, and the dependence restrictions that make the region informative are themselves assumptions nobody can check. The joint region is typically not a product of the marginal regions, so the computationally convenient answer is also the wrong one, and the correct one can be uninformative. Reporting a wide identification region is professionally costly, since it makes an honest analysis look weaker than a naive one and no journal requires it.
problems.proposed_direction: Extend the existing joint multi-bias machinery to include practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods, which is the violation current joint analyses omit. Specify compatible bias parameters and explicit dependence restrictions, state the target population and estimand, and report the partial-identification set separately from the sampling interval so a reader can see which part more data would reduce. Establish by simulation how far the product of marginal sensitivity analyses misstates the joint region, since that approximation is the current default.
